research_question: Is there a scientific basis to the Meridian System in traditional Chinese medicine?

selected_primary_idea.title: Meridian Residual Specificity Trial: A Pre-Registered Multimodal Test of Canonical Trajectories Against Matched Anatomical Controls
selected_primary_idea.summary: Test whether canonical meridian labels explain reproducible residual variance after known anatomy, tissue properties, stimulation characteristics, expectancy, and spatial dependence are controlled.
selected_primary_idea.scientific_object: A blinded coordinate representation of canonical traditional meridian trajectories, compared with anatomy-matched and spatially shifted coordinates.
mechanism_model: canonical labels may be entirely reducible to known anatomy and generic somatosensory physiology
canonical labels may index a reproducible physical or physiological feature not captured by measured anatomical covariates
measurement artifacts may create apparent path signals
falsification_criteria: No out-of-sample canonical-label increment after covariate adjustment.
Effects are explained by tissue depth, collagen proxies, contact quality, or regional anatomy.
validation_structure: independent replication before any ontological conclusion

competitive_ideas.title: Multi-Scale Atlas of Canonical Paths and Known Anatomy
competitive_ideas.reason_not_selected: Useful for measurement planning but cannot alone establish specificity.

competitive_ideas.title: Evidence-Graph Audit of Meridian, Mechanism, and Clinical Claims
competitive_ideas.reason_not_selected: Improves traceability but cannot resolve biological specificity without empirical data.

high_risk_ideas.title: Predictive Comparison of Canonical and Anatomy-Based Point Prescriptions
high_risk_ideas.risk: Clinical heterogeneity and ethical requirements make causal interpretation of a meridian ontology weak.

rejected_ideas.title: Infer meridian existence from any observed acupuncture benefit
rejected_ideas.reason: Violates the Survey distinction between outcome efficacy and channel ontology.

rejected_ideas.title: Declare interstitial spaces to be the meridians
rejected_ideas.reason: Treats an interpretive hypothesis as a uniquely validated anatomical identification.

mcts_evolution_summary.defect: The original question is ontologically broad and vulnerable to visual pattern matching.
mcts_evolution_summary.revision: Split into clinical, physiological, and meridian-specific claims.

mcts_evolution_summary.defect: Simple point-versus-nonpoint comparisons confound ordinary anatomy.
mcts_evolution_summary.revision: Require anatomy-matched and spatially shifted controls.
Adopt preregistered multimodal residual testing with held-out trajectories.
